nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm, bright sun drives year-round growth in the lowland Terai, from sal canopy to river algae.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Summer monsoon rains feed the rivers and make the grasses and forest grow tall.

nodes.name: River floods
nodes.desc: Monsoon floods and erosion along the Rapti and Narayani keep reshaping banks and sandbars, opening new ground for kans grass.

nodes.name: Grassland fires
nodes.desc: Seasonal bushfires burn off old grass in the park, and fresh growth follows for grazers such as gaur.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, dead grass and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil and river.

nodes.name: Sal
nodes.desc: The dominant tree of the park, making up about 70 percent of the cover and forming the purest stands in the central lowlands.

nodes.name: Kans grass
nodes.desc: A tall grass that is among the first plants to colonise fresh sandbanks. Tall grasslands cover roughly a fifth of the park.

nodes.name: Sickle senna
nodes.desc: A common weedy shrub of the park area. GloBI records show chital and sambar eating it.

nodes.name: River algae
nodes.desc: Green algae growing in the slow rivers, oxbow lakes and pools, the base of the aquatic food chain.

nodes.name: Termites
nodes.desc: Mound-building insects that eat dead plant matter. Sloth bears dig into their mounds and eat them.

nodes.name: Indian rhinoceros
nodes.desc: A grazer of tall alluvial grasslands that also eats leaves, fruits and water plants. Chitwan holds most of Nepal's rhinos.

nodes.name: Asian elephant
nodes.desc: A huge grazer and browser of grass, leaves and bark that moves through forest and grassland.

nodes.name: Hog deer
nodes.desc: A small deer of the floodplain grasslands, recorded as prey of tigers and leopards.

nodes.name: Chital
nodes.desc: The most common deer in the park, grazing and browsing and feeding tigers, leopards, jackals and crocodiles.

nodes.name: Sambar
nodes.desc: A large forest deer that browses and grazes. A favoured prey of tigers.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots for seeds, roots and invertebrates. Prey for tigers and leopards.

nodes.name: River fish
nodes.desc: The Rapti-Narayani river system has over a hundred fish species, which feed gharials and mugger crocodiles.

nodes.name: Sloth bear
nodes.desc: Eats termites and ants, plus fruit and honey. Chitwan is said to hold a high density of them. Tigers are its main predator.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: An opportunistic hunter and scavenger, recorded eating deer and wild boar.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: Commonest on the park edges, where tigers are less dominant. Takes deer, boar and smaller prey.

nodes.name: Mugger crocodile
nodes.desc: Eats mainly fish but also snakes, birds and mammals up to chital size. Shares the Rapti and Narayani with gharials.

nodes.name: Gharial
nodes.desc: A fish-eating crocodilian with a narrow snout. Wild numbers crashed and a breeding centre in the park has released young into the rivers since 1981.

nodes.name: Bengal tiger
nodes.desc: The top predator of the park. Hunts deer and wild boar, and also takes sloth bears and leopards.
